segments.title: Cold Open & Hype Train Check-In
segments.notes: Case and Pepito banter about Madeline books and hats; Hype Train arrives sick with 'hype pus' and auto-tuned, derails into sleepiness before completing.

segments.title: Gaza Hospital Raid Check-In with Rick
segments.notes: Rick (claiming former CIA) reads Reuters report on Israeli raid of Nasser Hospital; repeatedly attributes casualties to Hamas-run sources; frames surgical strikes as 'hospital stuff'; helicopters out to DJ Newsic's roof.

segments.title: Trailer Block: X-Men '97, Trash Humpers, Thundermans, AI Popeye
segments.notes: Trent watches X-Men '97 trailer, Harmony Korine's Trash Humpers, The Thundermans Return, and an AI-generated Will Smith Popeye trailer debunked by local news.

segments.title: Debate: Robin Williams vs Will Smith as Popeye
segments.notes: Crum returns from 'MIA' week; argues for Will Smith; Munch defends Robin Williams (who actually played Popeye); chat votes Robin Williams; Munch reveals 6-day Raising Cane's streak.

segments.title: British Bodybuilder Eats Four Sticks of Butter Daily; Bob Pepper Impersonates Bob Shepard
segments.notes: Peter Gibbon and Chat read NY Post story on Jonathan Griffiths' butter/meat diet; Case brings up Bob Shepard interview but gets Bob Pepper (gumballs announcer) instead; Pepper rants about silent baseball, mackerel crackers, punt hunts.

segments.title: Chernobyl Mutant Wolves Develop Cancer Resistance
segments.notes: Jeff Ripple reports on Princeton ecotoxicologist study: wolves in exclusion zone show altered immune systems after 11.28 mrem/day radiation; commenters share folk wisdom on eggs, butter, government spelling.

segments.title: Delta Flight Maggot Infestation; Bob Pepper Baseball Rap; Raid to Ricky Pika
segments.notes: Kendall joins on roof to dissect Valentine's dinner; DJ Newsic sings maggot plane story; Bob Pepper raps over 'Take Me Out to the Ball Game' beat; Case raids Ricky Pika.

characters.name: Pepito
characters.notes: executive producer. Opens show asleep; refuses hats due to hair condition; denies butter to Peter; produces Bob Pepper mix-up.

characters.name: Hype Train
characters.notes: recurring. Arrives sick with 'hype pus' in smokestack; auto-tuned; falls asleep mid-rant; completes train.

characters.name: Kendelle
characters.notes: in-studio contributor. Woken for Valentine's dinner debrief; later joins DJ Newsic on roof to detail service failures and near-proposal.

characters.name: Trent
characters.notes: correspondent. Hosts trailer block from 'at the movies'; reacts to X-Men '97, Trash Humpers, Thundermans, AI Popeye.

characters.name: Munch (Ralph Munchcut)
characters.notes: debate analyst. Returns to debate desk; defends Robin Williams as Popeye; reveals 6-day Raising Cane's breakfast/lunch/dinner streak.

characters.name: Crum (Leonard Crum)
characters.notes: debate analyst. Returns after week of sending siblings; argues for Will Smith Popeye; claims family wins count for score.

characters.name: Peter Gibbon
characters.notes: news stowaway. Suggests butter bodybuilder story; claims butter stash in walls; reads NY Post piece with Chat.

characters.name: Jeff Ripple
characters.notes: correspondent. Delivers Chernobyl wolf study; reads commenters' folk nutrition takes; signs off as 'Big Ripple'.

characters.name: DJ Newsic
characters.notes: recurring. Hosts musical finale from roof; sings maggot plane parody; struggles with beat selection; brings Bob Pepper for baseball rap.

characters.name: Bob Pepper
characters.notes: call-in guest. Impersonates deceased Yankees PA announcer Bob Shepard; rants about silent baseball, mackerel crackers, punt hunts; raps over baseball beat.

lore_notes.fact: Ate Raising Cane's for breakfast, lunch, and dinner six days in a row.
Removed shirt on camera to display physique during butter bodybuilder story.
Impersonated Bob Shepard (died 2010) claiming to be 'Bob Pepper, New Jersey Gumballs announcer, 78 years young.'
Joined DJ Newsic segment from roof to recount Valentine's dinner service failures and near-proposal moment.

episode_summary: Barely Informed News opened with a sickly Hype Train before pivoting to a grim Gaza hospital raid check-in delivered by self-proclaimed former CIA asset Rick. The broadcast lightened into a trailer block, a heated Munch & Crum debate over Popeye casting (Robin Williams won), a British bodybuilder's four-stick butter diet, and a botched Bob Shepard interview that yielded gumballs announcer Bob Pepper. Jeff Ripple reported Chernobyl wolves' radiation resistance, then DJ Newsic closed with a maggot-infested Delta flight musical and a baseball rap from Pepper before raiding Ricky Pika.
